question: persister
prompt:
Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Here are 5 ideas that were proposed for this question:

1. Barcoded lineage tracing with drug pulses: Label each founder cell with a unique heritable DNA barcode, expose the population to the targeted drug, and sequence barcodes in survivors versus the pre-treatment pool. Shared barcodes across survivors reveal whether persisters are pre-existing, clonally selected, or arise from a non-genetic switch in many cells. Adding washout and re-challenge arms tests whether the surviving state is reversible.
2. Single-cell multi-omics time course during treatment: Profile scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq (or multiome) on cells at baseline, early after drug exposure, and at several later timepoints, then compare the trajectories of cells that die with those that persist. Pre-treatment states that predict survival, such as chromatin accessibility at lineage or stress genes, can be identified and tested for causality.
3. Live-cell reporter imaging linked to fate: Use fluorescent reporters for cell cycle (e.g., FUCCI), stress signaling (e.g., NF-κB or p53 activity), or a drug-target pathway readout, and track individual cells with time-lapse microscopy through treatment. Retrospectively correlating each cell's reporter dynamics before and during drug exposure with its eventual death or survival reveals the dynamic signatures that distinguish persisters.
4. Pooled CRISPR screen comparing survivors with the bulk population: Run genome-wide or epigenome-focused CRISPR knockout or CRISPRi screens under drug treatment and sequence guides in survivors versus untreated controls. Genes whose loss either eliminates or enriches persisters point to the regulators of tolerance, and follow-up with arrayed validation can separate primary survival mechanisms from bystander effects.
5. Metabolic and epigenetic state profiling of sorted persisters: Sort out drug-tolerant cells from a reporter or viability-based gate and profile them for mitochondrial function, metabolite levels, histone modifications, and chromatin accessibility compared with sensitive cells. Testing whether pharmacologically perturbing the identified pathway (for example, OXPHOS inhibition or a histone demethylase inhibitor) changes survival fraction would establish whether the state is functionally necessary.

A senior expert reviewing them says they are the ideas everyone in the field would propose first. Propose 5 replacement ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that are substantially less obvious but still concrete, scientifically sound, and feasible for a research lab. Do not repeat or lightly modify the ideas above. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Sort by intracellular drug content, not by reporter state
ideas.description: Measure each cell's drug load with a clickable or fluorescent drug analog, or by LC-MS on FACS-sorted fractions, then compare survival of low- and high-accumulation cells at matched target engagement. This separates pharmacokinetic heterogeneity (efflux, uptake, sequestration) from genuine target-based tolerance.

ideas.title: Mitochondrial genome swap via cybrids
ideas.description: Fuse enucleated cytoplasts from survivor-enriched clones into a rho0 nuclear background carrying sensitive-clone nuclei, and reciprocally. If drug survival follows the mtDNA rather than the nuclear genotype, mitochondrial genome variation is causal, a test that is rarely run in persister studies.

ideas.title: Spatial niche mapping in drug-treated spheroids
ideas.description: Use multiplexed imaging (e.g., CODEX or MERFISH) on spheroids at 24–72 h of treatment, registering each surviving cell to local hypoxia, nutrient, and necrotic-core gradients. Then test the spatially enriched niche by reproducing it in controlled hypoxia or nutrient gradient devices to see whether it causes survival.

ideas.title: Pulse-duration by dose matrix with a mechanistic transition model
ideas.description: Expose cultures to a grid of drug concentrations and pulse durations, measure survivor fractions over time, and fit an ODE model with explicit rates for death, dormancy entry, and reawakening. Model-selected rates then predict the outcome of untested schedules, inferring the switching mechanism without lineage labels.

ideas.title: Asymmetric inheritance of proteostasis damage at first mitosis
ideas.description: Label a drug-induced aggregate or chaperone reporter with HaloTag and pulse-chase it through the first post-treatment division, then track which daughter inherits the damaged load. If daughters receiving less damage are the ones that persist, segregation of proteotoxic burden at mitosis is a candidate determinant of survival.
